Framing the March 20, 2019 FOMC statement through the January 2019 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) lens modestly deepens the Committee’s patient, cautious stance. The SLOOS shows banks tightening standards and other terms for C&I (including construction and land development), reporting wider loan rate spreads and weaker demand across business credit, and expecting tighter standards and softer business loan demand in 2019. Banks also anticipated some deterioration in loan performance (notably mortgages and nonprime consumer), while standards for several household categories (GSE-eligible mortgages, HELOCs, auto) were largely unchanged.

These credit-supply and demand headwinds reinforce the FOMC’s observations of slower household spending and business investment and muted inflation pressures, supporting a hold on rates and continued reinvestments. Relative to the statement alone, the SLOOS tilts the tone a bit more dovish, though still balanced by the overall resilience of the financial system.
